children: The gauge for China's factory activity is likely to indicate improvement in November, according to Goldman Sachs in a research note. GS expects official manufacturing purchasing managers' index to edge up to 49.5 in November from 49.3 in October. A PMI reading below 50 signals contraction in activity. The improvement is supported by high-frequency indicators, such as steel production, which rose sequentially during the month, the bank says. It also expects the RatingDog manufacturing PMI, compiled by S&P Global, to rise to 52.2 in November from 52.0 in October, supported by stronger port activity in coastal regions compared with last month. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
